title: Applying the magnitude-gap filter before matching raised the larger-first share in shallow ComCat pairs in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested the order of two selection steps in earthquake pair analysis. We used a fixed global ComCat M5.5+ snapshot. Both events had depth below 70 km, distance at most 200 km in three dimensions, and a time gap of 1 to below 30 days. Rule A made shortest-gap disjoint matches, then required an absolute magnitude difference of at least 0.5. Rule B applied that magnitude test before matching. In 2013-2025, A gave 134 larger-first pairs out of 255 (52.5%), while B gave 256 out of 423 (60.5%). The paired increase was 8.0 percentage points, with a conditional 95% graph-bootstrap interval of 3.3 to 12.5. In 2000-2012 the increase was 6.9 points, with limits of 2.5 to 11.3. All five rule checks in each era gave positive point changes. Both rules prevent event reuse and preserve time-reversal symmetry. The difference therefore shows selection sensitivity within disjoint matching. This extends prior campaign filter-order checks with a direct paired comparison at a lower entry threshold over two eras. It does not identify triggered events or a physical cause. One revised catalog, mixed magnitude types, greedy matching and group independence assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate group counts, provenance, scalar audits and a figure are included. External event records are excluded.

display.caption: Filter order changes the larger-first share. Left: primary estimates in two eras. Right: paired later-era changes for every rule. Bars give conditional 95% graph-bootstrap limits.

citations.reason: Prior shallow disjoint-pair study already included a gap-first check. We test the direct paired filter-order contrast over two eras at M5.5. Data overlap; no independent catalog replication is claimed.
We reuse the published shallow reference definition and fixed eras. Primary A counts agree exactly.
Exact reciprocal cancellation explains why pair direction differs from pooled equal-threshold before-after counts.
